en: The Philippine eagle, also called the monkey-eating eagle, is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the forests of the Philippines.
The waling-waling, scientifically known as Vanda sanderiana, is a highly prized epiphytic orchid native to the moist forests of Mindanao.
Filipino pediatrician Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide affordable neonatal care in rural areas without electricity.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine ecosystem hosting hundreds of coral and fish species.
The Philippine tarsier has specialized eyes that are as large as its brain, allowing it to see clearly in the dark.
Mangrove trees like Rhizophora have specialized stilt roots that anchor them in soft mud and filter out excess salt from seawater.
The BCG vaccine, given to newborns in the Philippines, protects infants from severe forms of tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium bacteria.
Donsol in Sorsogon serves as a critical feeding ground for the whale shark, the largest living fish species in the ocean.
Hemoglobin is the iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the human body.
The cacao tree, scientifically named Theobroma cacao, produces large seed pods directly on its trunk and branches in a process called cauliflory.
The monarch butterfly undergoes complete metamorphosis, transforming from a caterpillar to a chrysalis before finally emerging as an adult insect.
French physician Rene Laennec invented the stethoscope in 1816 to listen to internal body sounds without pressing his ear to the chest.
